title: Fleetscope / Capacity
description: Is ClickHouse keeping up with the fleet? Rows sent vs rows written, memory and CPU against the limits, scaling events and the ClickHouse Cloud trial credits. Times are UTC (billing days are UTC).

target.rawSql:
-- A row where the memory limit, CPU limit or replica count differs from the previous minute with data.
WITH
    per_minute AS
    (
        SELECT
            toStartOfMinute(event_time) AS minute,
            nullIf(maxIfOrNull(value, metric = 'CGroupMemoryTotal'), 0) / 1073741824 AS mem_limit_gib,
            nullIf(maxIfOrNull(value, metric = 'CGroupMaxCPU'), 0) AS cpu_limit_cores,
            uniqExactIf(hostname, metric = 'Uptime') AS replicas
        FROM system.asynchronous_metric_log
        WHERE event_time >= toStartOfMinute($__fromTime) - INTERVAL 1 MINUTE AND event_time <= $__toTime
          AND metric IN ('CGroupMemoryTotal', 'CGroupMaxCPU', 'Uptime')
        GROUP BY minute
    ),
    with_previous AS
    (
        SELECT
            minute,
            mem_limit_gib,
            cpu_limit_cores,
            replicas,
            lagInFrame(mem_limit_gib) OVER w AS prev_mem_limit_gib,
            lagInFrame(cpu_limit_cores) OVER w AS prev_cpu_limit_cores,
            lagInFrame(replicas) OVER w AS prev_replicas,
            row_number() OVER (ORDER BY minute) AS n
        FROM per_minute
        WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY minute ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
    )
SELECT
    minute AS time,
    arrayStringConcat(arrayFilter(part -> part != '',
    [
        if(ifNull(mem_limit_gib, -1) != ifNull(prev_mem_limit_gib, -1),
            concat('memory limit ', ifNull(toString(round(prev_mem_limit_gib, 2)), 'none'), ' → ',
                   ifNull(toString(round(mem_limit_gib, 2)), 'none'), ' GiB'), ''),
        if(ifNull(cpu_limit_cores, -1) != ifNull(prev_cpu_limit_cores, -1),
            concat('CPU limit ', ifNull(toString(round(prev_cpu_limit_cores, 2)), 'none'), ' → ',
                   ifNull(toString(round(cpu_limit_cores, 2)), 'none'), ' cores'), ''),
        if(replicas != prev_replicas, concat('replicas ', toString(prev_replicas), ' → ', toString(replicas)), '')
    ]), '; ') AS text
FROM with_previous
WHERE n > 1 AND minute >= toStartOfMinute($__fromTime) AND text != ''
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Rows sent vs rows written per minute ↗
panels.description: Rows the fleet sent (green, counted in actions, resource_samples, network_requests and issues) and rows ClickHouse wrote for them (blue, NewPart rows of system.part_log), per minute, all sources (system tables know no source or engine filter). Sent is placed by the event time and written by the time ClickHouse received it, so per minute the lines follow each other but do not match exactly; over an hour they do. The lines follow each other; in a single minute they can differ at the edges. A minute with no rows is 0. Click to open Sessions with this range.

targets.rawSql:
-- Rows the fleet sent vs rows ClickHouse wrote (system.part_log), and sessions started, per minute; all sources.
SELECT
    minute AS time,
    sum(rows_sent) AS rows_sent,
    sum(rows_written) AS rows_written,
    sum(sessions_started) AS sessions_started
FROM
(
    SELECT toStartOfMinute(ts) AS minute, count() AS rows_sent, toUInt64(0) AS rows_written, toUInt64(0) AS sessions_started
    FROM actions
    WHERE ts >= toStartOfMinute($__fromTime) AND ts <= $__toTime
    GROUP BY minute
    UNION ALL
    SELECT toStartOfMinute(ts), count(), 0, 0
    FROM resource_samples
    WHERE ts >= toStartOfMinute($__fromTime) AND ts <= $__toTime
    GROUP BY 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT toStartOfMinute(ts), count(), 0, 0
    FROM network_requests
    WHERE ts >= toStartOfMinute($__fromTime) AND ts <= $__toTime
    GROUP BY 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT toStartOfMinute(ts), count(), 0, 0
    FROM issues
    WHERE ts >= toStartOfMinute($__fromTime) AND ts <= $__toTime
    GROUP BY 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT toStartOfMinute(started_at), 0, 0, count()
    FROM sessions FINAL
    WHERE started_at >= toStartOfMinute($__fromTime) AND started_at <= $__toTime
    GROUP BY 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT toDateTime(toStartOfMinute(event_time), 'UTC'), 0, sum(rows), 0
    FROM system.part_log
    WHERE event_type = 'NewPart'
      AND database = currentDatabase()
      AND error = 0
      AND `table` IN ('actions', 'resource_samples', 'network_requests', 'issues')
      AND event_time >= toStartOfMinute($__fromTime) AND event_time <= $__toTime
    GROUP BY 1
)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time WITH FILL FROM toStartOfMinute($__fromTime) TO $__toTime STEP 60

panels.title: Difference, last hour ↗
panels.description: |rows written − rows sent| as a percentage of rows sent, all sources, over the 60 whole minutes that ended a minute ago (the time picker does not change it). About 0% is good: ClickHouse writes what the fleet sends. Yellow from 1%, red from 5%. — means nothing was sent or written. Click to open Sessions for the last hour.

targets.rawSql:
-- Rows written vs rows sent over the last 60 whole minutes, |difference| as % of sent (NULL when idle).
WITH
    toStartOfMinute(now()) - INTERVAL 1 MINUTE AS window_end,
    window_end - INTERVAL 60 MINUTE AS window_start,
    (SELECT count() FROM actions WHERE ts >= window_start AND ts < window_end)
        + (SELECT count() FROM resource_samples WHERE ts >= window_start AND ts < window_end)
        + (SELECT count() FROM network_requests WHERE ts >= window_start AND ts < window_end)
        + (SELECT count() FROM issues WHERE ts >= window_start AND ts < window_end) AS sent,
    (
        SELECT sum(rows)
        FROM system.part_log
        WHERE event_type = 'NewPart'
          AND database = currentDatabase()
          AND error = 0
          AND `table` IN ('actions', 'resource_samples', 'network_requests', 'issues')
          AND event_time >= window_start AND event_time < window_end
    ) AS written
SELECT multiIf(
    sent = 0 AND written = 0, NULL,
    sent = 0, 100,
    100 * abs(toInt64(written) - toInt64(sent)) / sent) AS value

panels.title: How to read this
panels.description: What the colours and the sections mean.

options.content: All sources, real and simulated. Green: sent. Blue: written or used. Grey: a limit. Yellow: sessions. Not available is never 0.

panels.title: Memory, % of limit
panels.description: The highest memory use of any replica in the last 10 minutes, as a percentage of that replica's memory limit (the time picker does not change it). Yellow from 70%, red from 85%. Not available when the server reports no limit (a local container has none).

targets.rawSql:
-- Highest memory use of any replica in the last 10 minutes, as % of its limit (NULL without a limit).
SELECT maxOrNull(pct) AS value
FROM
(
    SELECT
        100 * maxIfOrNull(value, metric = 'CGroupMemoryUsed')
            / nullIf(maxIfOrNull(value, metric = 'CGroupMemoryTotal'), 0) AS pct
    FROM system.asynchronous_metric_log
    WHERE event_time >= now() - INTERVAL 10 MINUTE
      AND metric IN ('CGroupMemoryUsed', 'CGroupMemoryTotal')
    GROUP BY toStartOfMinute(event_time), hostname
)

panels.title: CPU, % of limit
panels.description: The average CPU of the busiest replica over the last 10 minutes, as a percentage of its core limit (the time picker does not change it). Yellow from 70%, red from 85%. Not available when the server reports no CPU limit (a local container has none).

targets.rawSql:
-- Average CPU of the busiest replica in the last 10 minutes, as % of its core limit (NULL without a limit).
SELECT maxOrNull(pct) AS value
FROM
(
    SELECT
        100 * (avgIfOrNull(value, metric = 'CGroupUserTime') + avgIfOrNull(value, metric = 'CGroupSystemTime'))
            / nullIf(maxIfOrNull(value, metric = 'CGroupMaxCPU'), 0) AS pct
    FROM system.asynchronous_metric_log
    WHERE event_time >= now() - INTERVAL 10 MINUTE
      AND metric IN ('CGroupUserTime', 'CGroupSystemTime', 'CGroupMaxCPU')
    GROUP BY hostname
)

panels.title: Replicas
panels.description: Replicas that logged in the latest minute of the time range. System tables are per replica, so this is the replica Grafana reaches: 1 today, as we run one replica (see packages/db/README.md, One replica).

targets.rawSql:
-- Replicas that logged the Uptime metric, per minute.
SELECT
    toStartOfMinute(event_time) AS time,
    uniqExact(hostname) AS replicas
FROM system.asynchronous_metric_log
WHERE event_time >= toStartOfMinute($__fromTime) AND event_time <= $__toTime
  AND metric = 'Uptime'
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Replicas over time
panels.description: Replicas that logged in each minute (the replica Grafana reaches; we run one). A step marks a scale-up or scale-down; a gap means the server logged nothing.

targets.rawSql:
-- Replicas that logged the Uptime metric, per minute.
SELECT
    toStartOfMinute(event_time) AS time,
    uniqExact(hostname) AS replicas
FROM system.asynchronous_metric_log
WHERE event_time >= toStartOfMinute($__fromTime) AND event_time <= $__toTime
  AND metric = 'Uptime'
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Memory, used vs limit
panels.description: All sources. Peak memory of the server's container in each minute (blue) against its memory limit (grey line), in GiB, per replica. A missing limit is a gap (a local container has none), never 0. Grey markers on the chart are scaling changes.

targets.rawSql:
-- Memory and CPU of the server against its limits, per minute and replica; a missing limit is NULL.
SELECT
    toStartOfMinute(event_time) AS time,
    splitByChar('.', hostname)[1] AS replica,
    maxIfOrNull(value, metric = 'CGroupMemoryUsed') / 1073741824 AS mem_used_gib,
    nullIf(maxIfOrNull(value, metric = 'CGroupMemoryTotal'), 0) / 1073741824 AS mem_limit_gib,
    avgIfOrNull(value, metric = 'CGroupUserTime') + avgIfOrNull(value, metric = 'CGroupSystemTime') AS cpu_used_cores,
    nullIf(maxIfOrNull(value, metric = 'CGroupMaxCPU'), 0) AS cpu_limit_cores
FROM system.asynchronous_metric_log
WHERE event_time >= toStartOfMinute($__fromTime) AND event_time <= $__toTime
  AND metric IN ('CGroupMemoryUsed', 'CGroupMemoryTotal', 'CGroupUserTime', 'CGroupSystemTime', 'CGroupMaxCPU')
GROUP BY time, replica
ORDER BY time, replica

panels.title: Credits used since 2026-10-24
panels.description: Sum of totalCHC over all entities from the ClickHouse Cloud usage API, from 2026-10-24 (the start of the trial) to today. The newest days may not be final yet. Billing reads the ClickHouse Cloud API through the Infinity data source `clickhouse-cloud-api`, which needs the API key; without it (local, CI) this panel shows no data.

panels.title: Credits left of $300
panels.description: $300 minus the credits used since 2026-10-24. Assumes 1 credit = $1. Billing reads the ClickHouse Cloud API through the Infinity data source `clickhouse-cloud-api`, which needs the API key; without it (local, CI) this panel shows no data.

panels.title: Projected run-out vs trial end
panels.description: The date the credits run out (trial ends 2026-11-23) if the next days cost what the last 3 full days cost on average (today is not counted), and how many days before or after the trial end (2026-11-23) that is. ▲ red: runs out before the trial ends. ✓ green: lasts through the trial end. Billing reads the ClickHouse Cloud API through the Infinity data source `clickhouse-cloud-api`, which needs the API key; without it (local, CI) this panel shows no data.

panels.title: Credits per day, last 30 days
panels.description: ClickHouse credits (totalCHC) spent each day over the last 30 days, from the ClickHouse Cloud usage API, summed over all services and entities of the day. The newest days may not be final yet. Billing reads the ClickHouse Cloud API through the Infinity data source `clickhouse-cloud-api`, which needs the API key; without it (local, CI) this panel shows no data.
